question.problem: If $\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta =-\frac{1}{7}$ and ${180}^{∘}<\theta <{270}^{∘},$ then what is the value of $\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta ?$
question.worked_solution:
Let's sketch our angle $\theta $ in the coordinate plane.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14263705/assets/143519dfc291a32f5c617b70a4297643429b18eea64b7ad4736758c60c3a7e27.png)

We're given that $\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta =-\frac{1}{7}$ We can use the Pythagorean identity to find $\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta :$

$$
\begin{aligned}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1 \\ {cos}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1-{sin}^{2}⁡\theta  \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta =-\frac{1}{7}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{(-\frac{1}{7})}^{2}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{1-\frac{1}{49}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{48}{49}} \\  & =\pm \frac{4\sqrt{3}}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$

We select the negative answer since $\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $ is negative in the third quadrant. So, $\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta =-\frac{4\sqrt{3}}{7}.$

Finally, knowing that $\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta },$ we have

$$
\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta =\frac{(-\frac{4\sqrt{3}}{7})}{(-\frac{1}{7})}=4\sqrt{3}.
$$
